messages.content: "請先幫忙檢索大都會藝術博物館中排名前十的熱門藝術品，按照受歡迎程度排序，然後再檢索排名前五的藝術品，按照年代排序。之後，能否搜尋從2020年1月1日開始在加州提起的與Google有關的正在進行中的訴訟？最後，也能否找到從2018年1月1日開始在紐約提起的與Microsoft有關的已解決訴訟？"

function.name: metropolitan_museum_get_top_artworks
function.description: Fetches the list of popular artworks at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Results can be sorted based on popularity. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

number.description: The number of artworks to fetch

sort_by.description: The criteria to sort the results on. Default is 'popularity'.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a specific company within a specific date range and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The company related to the lawsuit.

start_date.description: Start of the date range for when the lawsuit was filed.

location.description: Location where the lawsuit was filed.

status.description: The status of the lawsuit. Default is 'ongoing'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1) Retrieve top ten most popular artworks from Met museum sorted by popularity.

2) Then retrieve top five artworks sorted chronologically (i.e., earliest? but they say ranking front five; maybe just first five after sorting chronological). They want them separately.

We need to call the function twice with different parameters.

First call: get_top_artworks(number=10, sort_by="popularity")

Second call: get_top_artworks(number=5, sort_by="chronological") or alphabetical? But they said "按年代排序", so use chronological.

Then third request: search lawsuits involving Google starting Jan 1 2020 in California ongoing.

Call lawsuit_search(company='Google', start_date='2020-01-01', location='California', status='ongoing')

Fourth request: find lawsuits involving Microsoft since Jan 1 2018 in New York settled.

Call lawsuit_search(company='Microsoft', start_date='2018-01-01', location='NewYork'?? Actually location param expects string; we should pass 'New York'.

But note that the function signature says location: string. So we provide 'New York'.

Also default status is 'ongoing'; we override to 'settled'.

Thus four calls.

Now produce JSON array of objects each containing name and arguments. Use correct names as defined: metropolitan_museum_get_top_artworks and lawsuit_search.

Return only JSON array no other text. Ensure proper quoting etc. Let's craft.

JSON array:
[
 {"name":"metropolitan_museum_get_top_artworks","arguments":{"number":10,"sort_by":"popularity"}},
 {"name":"metropolitan_museum_get_top_artworks","arguments":{"number":5,"sort_by":"chronological"}},
 {"name":"lawsuit_search","arguments":{"company":"Google","start_date":"2020-01-01","location":"California","status":"ongoing"}},
 {"name":"lawsuit_search","arguments":{"company":"Microsoft","start_date":"2018-01-01","location":"New York","status":"settled"}}
]

Make sure keys match exactly. Provide output accordingly.
